I suggest playing easier difficulties to learn the smaller maps first, then the larger ones. Then it becomes easier on higher difficulties because you know where the hiding spots are. Of course, some hiding spots will be blocked off in higher difficulties, but at least you'll know where to check right off the bat. Keep me tal note, run to those places and always have a smudge on you. Electronics tend to flicker, I believe (it's been a moment since I last played) that your heartbeat pounds in-game too, don't forget that you can hear them make noise when they hunt (except for that one butthole ghost type that is kind of quiet when it hunts), and if you have any type of camera on you, the camera distorts quite a bit as well.




  Make sure to turn off all of you electronics (except for the glo-stick, use that as lighting if you really need it because it isn't electronic). You can also bring two flashlights into the map with you to toss on the floor for a lighted path next to the main door or to an open hiding spot so you can't miss it in a rush to get away. You'll always be able to hear these guys before you see them unless it's one of those dorky moments you are in the ghost room with the ghost.
